note: P1''' — the SECOND external-fact fixture for task-executor. Two facts live outside the artifact and only ONE of them is pointed at. (1) The store on disk is an envelope {v:1,items:[...]} and only src/store/json-store.js says so — the prompt NAMES that module, because structural §48 requires a brownfield prompt to say where the authoritative format lives, and without the pointer the shape would not be derivable from what the skill was given. That arm was therefore never SKIPPABLE: the fixture's own note claimed 'a file the model must choose to open' while its prompt said 'READ IT'. It ceilinged 1.0 on the first draft 3/3, and this is the likeliest reason. (2) R7 is the arm with NO pointer. src/store/compact.js writes the store file directly instead of going through json-store.write(), names every field it keeps, and archive uses it. A `tag` command written entirely correctly against read()/write() passes T1-T4 and R1-R6 and still loses every tag the first time anything is archived. Nothing `tag` touches imports compact.js, so finding it is a CHOICE — optional to producing a plausible artifact, which is exactly what dial three requires. DERIVABILITY (plan §0): the requirement is stated in the prompt — a tag stays attached, no other command may lose it — and the mechanism is documented in compact.js's own comment. The row is passable by reading the code the skill was handed; it is not passable by inferring how the harness probes. The renderer already displays tags in the SEEDED code, which does two things: it names the `tags` field so the skill is not graded on guessing it, and it makes R7 observable in one invocation regardless of where the skill chooses to render — archive prints what is left as it now stands on disk.
